task: Audit a report's Methods and 8 numbered results against the code and data, reporting every problem found.

planted_bugs.merge: Site D's session export writes unpadded IDs (D-7 against D-007), and ID normalization only fixes case and whitespace, so the inner join silently drops all of site D (N 395 instead of 429).
planted_bugs.reference_level: Education's category order is lost when written to CSV, so the model's reference is college, not secondary as the Methods says; 'graduate vs. secondary' is reported as 2.84 rather than 4.53 with both bugs fixed.
planted_bugs.stale_number: A typed training-group week-12 mean (57.4) left over from before a data correction (58.6 now). Planted wherever an arm's numbers are typed: the hand-written report (none), ASTRA findings' claim text, OpenResearch notes and report. Calkit's answers and report are filled in from results, so it can't occur there (null in 'found').

auditor.harness: Claude Code subagent, general-purpose, 3 per arm run one batch at a time, not told bugs existed, confined to its arm

orx logs metrics and data hashes traced result 3; short experiment IDs rejected; nothing links report to runs

conclusion: Every auditor found the merge bug, and the stale number every time it existed. The arms differed on the reference level (Calkit 3/3, ASTRA 3/3, none 2/3, OpenResearch 1/3), which with 3 runs each is suggestive at best. No framework was fastest, and each framework added time roughly in proportion to how much tool there was to navigate. Calkit prevented the stale number by construction. Every Calkit and ASTRA auditor called their tools' green checks false comfort, since they show outputs are current, not correct.
